project.name: canon_ball
project.description: Canon Ball is a Streamlit multipage app with two instruments: a semantic experiment runner that fires N trials with/without a knowledge layer and compares embedding distributions (UMAP, Mann-Whitney U), and Borges Graph, which builds autoregressive attribution circuits via the Neuronpedia Circuit Tracer with Lens and Mise-en-abîme visualization modes.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit landing page that bootstraps the Canon Ball multipage app, displaying project description and navigation to the two instrument pages.

nodes.name: borges_graph.py
nodes.summary: Implements the compiled attribution graph builder for Borges Graph, running an autoregressive loop that calls Neuronpedia Circuit Tracer at each generation step and accumulates a CompiledGraph of Step objects.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing one autoregressive generation step, holding the predicted token, its context length, the raw attribution response, and the pruned subgraph.

nodes.name: CompiledGraph
nodes.summary: Aggregates all autoregressive Step objects into a complete compiled attribution graph, exposing helpers to collect generated text, deduplicated feature IDs, and JSON serialization.

nodes.name: compile_attribution
nodes.summary: Main entry point for the Borges Graph instrument: drives the autoregressive loop, applies a sliding window to stay within the 64-token Circuit Tracer cap, and yields progress via an optional callback.

nodes.name: canon_analysis.py
nodes.summary: Provides all statistical analysis functions for the Canon Ball experiment: embedding collection, dispersion metrics (L2, cosine), pairwise distances, UMAP/t-SNE projection, and Mann-Whitney U group comparison.

nodes.name: compare_groups
nodes.summary: Compares control and test trial groups using per-trial centroids, Mann-Whitney U test on pairwise cosine distances, and centroid shift metrics.

nodes.name: project_2d
nodes.summary: Projects high-dimensional embeddings to 2D using UMAP or t-SNE, handling centroid projection separately for visualization in the Canon Ball dashboard.

nodes.name: full_analysis
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the complete analysis pipeline over an ExperimentRun, computing dispersion, pairwise distances, group comparison, 2D projection, and trial labels in one call.

nodes.name: canon_experiment.py
nodes.summary: Core experiment engine for Canon Ball: handles backend detection (Ollama vs OpenRouter), embedding via fastembed, four injection modes, trial execution, and JSON persistence of ExperimentRun results.

nodes.name: Trial
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing the result of a single LLM trial: raw output, token count, embeddings, and latency.

nodes.name: ExperimentRun
nodes.summary: Dataclass grouping all control and test trials from a single Canon Ball experiment run, including injection mode and timestamp.

nodes.name: assemble_messages
nodes.summary: Constructs the message list for a given injection mode (system_user, interleave, template, cot_priming) by interleaving prompt and knowledge-layer sentences.

nodes.name: run_experiment
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a full experiment run by executing N control and N test trials sequentially, reporting progress via an optional callback.

nodes.name: html_components.py
nodes.summary: Pure Python functions that return self-contained HTML/SVG/JS strings for the cannon animation, Mise-en-abîme triptych, and Lens optical-bench visualizations — no Streamlit dependency.

nodes.name: cannon_animation_html
nodes.summary: Generates a self-contained HTML/JS cannon animation widget with randomized projectile trajectories and a progress bar for the experiment run.

nodes.name: mise_en_abime_html
nodes.summary: Produces a three-panel Mise-en-abîme HTML triptych showing the knowledge layer, prompt attribution tree, and LLM reconstruction side by side with interactive hover highlighting.

nodes.name: lens_html
nodes.summary: Produces an optical-bench Lens visualization HTML widget with converging rays (knowledge features), a focal-point node (prompt features), and diverging rays (answer/context features).

nodes.name: neuronpedia_client.py
nodes.summary: Client library for the Neuronpedia API: provides NLA verbalization (batched, 16-position cap), attribution graph generation and pruning via Circuit Tracer, and scene-data builders for the Lens and Mise-en-abîme visualizations.

nodes.name: Feature
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a single SAE feature activation, including position, token, NLA description, and similarity scores.

nodes.name: NLAResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass wrapping a complete NLA verbalization response, including the list of Feature activations, model/source metadata, and error state.

nodes.name: verbalize_activations
nodes.summary: Runs NLA verbalization over a prompt, automatically batching across the 16-position API cap and returning an NLAResult with all Feature objects.

nodes.name: generate_attribution_graph
nodes.summary: Submits a prompt to the Neuronpedia Circuit Tracer endpoint and returns attribution graph metadata including S3 URL for subgraph fetching.

nodes.name: fetch_attribution_subgraph
nodes.summary: Downloads and prunes the attribution subgraph from S3, normalizing node depth, sorting by attribution weight, and preserving SAE feature identifiers for potential steering.

nodes.name: build_mise_en_abime_scene
nodes.summary: Builds the scene data dict for the Mise-en-abîme HTML component by aligning NLA features and attribution graph nodes to word positions in the prompt.

nodes.name: build_lens_scene
nodes.summary: Builds the scene data dict for the Lens HTML component by sorting features into converging (knowledge), focal (prompt), and diverging (answer) ray groups.

nodes.name: shared_sidebar.py
nodes.summary: Renders the shared Streamlit sidebar with prompt and knowledge layer text areas, persisting values to st.session_state for cross-page access.

nodes.name: render_shared_sidebar
nodes.summary: Renders the prompt and knowledge layer inputs in the Streamlit sidebar and syncs them to session state.

nodes.name: 1_Canon_Ball.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit page implementing the Canon Ball experiment dashboard: runs trials with/without knowledge layer, shows a cannon animation during execution, and renders UMAP scatter plots and statistical metrics.

nodes.name: 2_Borges_Graph.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit page implementing the Borges Graph instrument: triggers NLA verbalization and attribution graph computation, then renders the Lens or Mise-en-abîme visualization based on the selected display mode.

nodes.name: compute_scene
nodes.summary: Calls the Neuronpedia API to generate an attribution graph and fetch the subgraph, returning a mise-en-abîme scene dict.

nodes.name: render_scene
nodes.summary: Renders the selected visualization (Lens or Mise-en-abîme) into the Streamlit page using st.components.html, dispatching on the current display mode in session state.

nodes.name: config.toml
nodes.summary: Streamlit app configuration defining a dark theme and server settings for the Canon Ball multipage app.

nodes.name: secrets.toml.example
nodes.summary: Template for Streamlit secrets file documenting required API keys — OPENROUTER_API_KEY and NEURONPEDIA_API_KEY — for backend inference and Neuronpedia circuit tracing.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Python package dependencies listing Streamlit, sentence-transformers, fastembed, umap-learn, scipy, and other libraries required to run Canon Ball.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide for Claude Code describing the Canon Ball project architecture, how to run the app, module responsibilities, and key design constraints such as backend detection caching and Circuit Tracer token limits.

nodes.name: injection_mode_results.md
nodes.summary: Experiment results report (in French) documenting how each of the four knowledge-layer injection modes affects semantic dispersion and centroid shift in Canon Ball trials.

nodes.name: troubleshooting.md
nodes.summary: API contract reference and troubleshooting notes for the Neuronpedia NLA and Circuit Tracer endpoints, covering the 3-call loop, model constraints (gemma-2-2b, 64-token cap), CLTGraph JSON shape, and live verification results.

nodes.name: report.qmd
nodes.summary: Quarto document source for an experiment report analyzing injection mode effects on LLM output distributions, containing prose, code, and embedded visualizations.

nodes.name: report.html
nodes.summary: Rendered HTML export of the Canon Ball experiment report, generated from report.qmd and containing interactive charts, UMAP plots, and statistical analysis of injection mode results.

tour.title: Developer Guide & Architecture
tour.description: CLAUDE.md is the authoritative developer guide for this project, describing both instruments (Canon Ball and Borges Graph), how to run the app, each module's responsibility, and critical design constraints. Reading it first gives you the mental map you need before diving into the code — especially the distinction between the Streamlit UI layer and the backend library modules that have no Streamlit dependency.

tour.title: App Entry Point
tour.description: app.py is the Streamlit landing page that bootstraps the multipage application. It has zero fan-in (nothing imports it) and zero fan-out (it imports nothing) — Streamlit's multipage convention auto-discovers the pages/ directory, so the entry point is intentionally minimal. This file is the first thing Streamlit executes and the root from which both instruments branch off.
tour.languageLesson: Streamlit multipage apps use filesystem-based routing: any .py file placed in the pages/ directory becomes a separate page, named and ordered by its filename prefix. The root app.py acts as the landing page.

tour.title: Configuration & Secrets
tour.description: Before either instrument can run, two configuration files must be in place. config.toml sets the dark theme and server options for the Streamlit UI. secrets.toml.example is the template for the required API keys — OPENROUTER_API_KEY for the remote LLM backend and NEURONPEDIA_API_KEY for the Circuit Tracer. Copy it to secrets.toml and fill in your keys to unlock the full feature set.
tour.languageLesson: Streamlit reads secrets from .streamlit/secrets.toml at startup and exposes them as st.secrets['KEY']. This file must never be committed to version control — secrets.toml.example serves as a safe, committed template that documents which keys are needed.

tour.title: Shared Sidebar
tour.description: shared_sidebar.py is the cross-page state hub: it renders the sidebar's prompt text area and knowledge layer text area, then writes both values into st.session_state. Both instrument pages import it as their first act, so any input entered on one page is still there when the user navigates to the other. Its high fan-in (imported by both pages) makes it the most structurally central UI module in the project.
tour.languageLesson: st.session_state in Streamlit persists Python values across reruns and across page navigations within a session. Modules that write to session_state act as a shared memory layer between otherwise independent pages.

tour.title: Canon Ball Experiment Engine
tour.description: canon_experiment.py is the core domain logic for the first instrument. It handles backend detection (probing Ollama locally before falling back to OpenRouter), implements the four knowledge-injection modes (system_user, interleave, template, cot_priming), executes N trials, and persists results to results/experiment.json. Adding a new injection mode means adding an entry to INJECTION_MODES and a corresponding branch in the message-building logic here.
tour.languageLesson: The four injection modes are the core experimental variable of Canon Ball. Each mode places the knowledge layer at a different structural position in the LLM prompt, letting the experiment measure how injection position affects the semantic distribution of outputs.

tour.title: Statistical Analysis
tour.description: canon_analysis.py transforms raw trial outputs into interpretable statistics. It collects embeddings from the chosen backend, computes dispersion metrics (intra-group variance, centroid distance), projects outputs into 2D via UMAP or t-SNE for the scatter plot, and runs a Mann-Whitney U test to compare the with-knowledge and without-knowledge distributions. The results it produces are what the Canon Ball dashboard visualizes.

tour.title: Canon Ball Dashboard
tour.description: pages/1_Canon_Ball.py is the Streamlit page that ties the first instrument together. It imports shared_sidebar (user inputs), canon_experiment (trial runner), canon_analysis (stats), and html_components (animations and plots). When the user fires the cannon, this page orchestrates the full pipeline: run trials, compute embeddings, project with UMAP, render the scatter plot and Mann-Whitney metrics. It has the highest fan-out in the project (4 imports), making it the broadest integration point.

tour.title: Injection Mode Results
tour.description: injection_mode_results.md documents what actually happens when you run the experiment with the four injection modes. It records the measured semantic dispersion and centroid shift for each mode, making it the empirical companion to the code in canon_experiment.py. Read this alongside Step 5 to understand not just how the modes work but what they produce.

tour.title: Neuronpedia API Client
tour.description: neuronpedia_client.py is the API client layer shared by both the Borges Graph service and the Borges Graph page. It encapsulates all communication with Neuronpedia: batched NLA verbalization (capped at 16 token positions per request, automatically batched), attribution graph generation via the Circuit Tracer, graph pruning, and scene-data builders for the two visualization modes. Its high fan-in (imported by both borges_graph.py and the page) makes it the most important module to understand before tackling the Borges instrument.
tour.languageLesson: The 16-position-per-request cap on NLA explain is a hard API constraint. The client handles this transparently by splitting large token sequences into batches and merging the results — callers never need to know the cap exists.

tour.title: Attribution Graph Builder
tour.description: borges_graph.py implements the compiled attribution graph: an autoregressive loop where each iteration generates one token via sampling, calls the Neuronpedia Circuit Tracer to record the causal graph for that generation step, then appends the token to the growing context. The result is a CompiledGraph object that chains the per-step attribution graphs into a single structure, with SAE feature identifiers preserved for future steering experiments. A sliding window of ~60 tokens handles prompts that exceed the Circuit Tracer's 64-token cap.

tour.title: HTML Visualization Components
tour.description: html_components.py provides the visual layer for both instruments as pure Python functions that return HTML/SVG/JS strings. It renders the cannon animation for Canon Ball, the Lens optical-bench view (converge → focal → diverge mirror metaphor) and the Mise-en-abîme triptych for Borges Graph. Because it has no Streamlit import, these components can be tested and reused outside of Streamlit by passing the output to any HTML renderer.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping visualization logic Streamlit-free (returning raw HTML strings rather than calling st.components) is a deliberate design choice: it keeps the module testable in isolation and decouples the visual representation from the framework lifecycle.

tour.title: Borges Graph Dashboard
tour.description: pages/2_Borges_Graph.py is the Streamlit page for the second instrument. It imports shared_sidebar for the prompt input, neuronpedia_client for NLA verbalization and attribution graph computation, and html_components for the Lens or Mise-en-abîme rendering. The user selects a visualization mode, triggers computation, and the page wires the neuronpedia_client scene-data builders to the html_components renderers — the compiled graph from borges_graph.py feeds through neuronpedia_client before arriving here.

tour.title: Troubleshooting & API Reference
tour.description: troubleshooting.md is the practical companion to neuronpedia_client.py: it documents the exact API contracts for the NLA verbalization and Circuit Tracer endpoints, including known gotchas, rate limit behavior, and the model constraints (gemma-2-2b only for attribution, gemma-3-27b-it and llama3.3-70b-it only for NLA). When the Neuronpedia client returns unexpected results or errors, this is the first document to consult.

tour.title: Experiment Report
tour.description: report.qmd is the Quarto source document that compiles the full Canon Ball experiment analysis, and report.html is its rendered output. Together they represent the scientific artifact that the project produces: a reproducible report analyzing how the four injection modes affect LLM output distributions. The report bridges the raw results persisted by canon_experiment.py and the statistical measures computed by canon_analysis.py into a human-readable narrative.
